description: Idempotency keys (sections 7.2, 5.2 and 5.5), on a server client with the fake transport, where customer is customer("user_42"). Key cases pass key, exactly as given, as the caller's idempotencyKey, and length is its length in Unicode code points, for reading: recordUsage is customer.recordUsage("ai_credits", 1, { idempotencyKey }), holdUsage and startHold take the same arguments, withHold takes them with work, adjustMeter is customer.adjustMeter("ai_credits", { by: 1, idempotencyKey }) and cancel is customer.cancel({ idempotencyKey }). The fake transport answers the hold with a 200 UsageResult whose outcome is held, with amount 1 and a hold id, the settlement with outcome settled, and the excess report with outcome recorded. startHold's handle and withHold's work report use(2) and then finish, so 1 is settled and the excess of 1 is recorded with recordUsage, whose Idempotency-Key is excessKey. A key of null makes the call with no idempotencyKey. customer.token(), customer.snapshot(), customer.billingPortal({ returnUrl: "https://app.example.com/billing" }) and customer.syncBilling() take no key, so their key is null. outcome is the exact argument error, raised before any request, or valid: the request sends key as Idempotency-Key or, when key is null, a new UUID v4 (version 4, variant 10) of its own, so making the call twice sends two different keys; a valid startHold or withHold case adds excessKey. Batch cases call recordUsageBatch(events, { register }), passing no register when register is null, which never throws, with events as given or expanded from eventPattern in order: event i, counted from 0 to count − 1, is { customer: customerPrefix followed by i mod customers in decimal, feature, amount: i + 1, idempotencyKey: keyPrefix followed by i in decimal }, with no occurredAt, and overrides replaces the event at each index with its event. A batch outcome gives refused, the events the SDK answers error without sending them (each with its index, counted from 0, its code and its message; an event with several faults is answered with the first of customer, feature, amount and key), and requests, each request sent, in order, with its number of events, serialised (the exact JSON array section 5.2 hashes, written as section 7.3 writes cache keys, with occurredAt as sent, in UTC with milliseconds, or null) and idempotencyKey (batch: followed by the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of serialised). The answers to those requests are not compared. calls, where present, makes the same batch call that many times, and each call sends the same requests. A case with appliesWhere runs only where that holds.

refused.message: Pass idempotencyKey: a key from your own unit of work, such as a message or job id.

cases.name: batch-event-blank-customer
cases.why: An event with an empty customer is answered error with invalid_body and customer(id)'s blank message, and nothing is sent.

refused.message: Provide the id your app uses for the customer.

cases.name: batch-event-whitespace-customer
cases.why: A customer of only a space and a tab is blank, so the event is answered error with invalid_body.

refused.message: Provide the id your app uses for the customer.

cases.name: batch-event-blank-feature
cases.why: An event with an empty feature is answered error with invalid_body and the feature's blank message.

refused.message: Name the feature by its key.

cases.name: batch-event-amount-zero
cases.why: An amount of 0 is below 1, so the event is answered error with invalid_amount.

refused.message: Pass amount as a whole number from 1 to 9007199254740991.

cases.name: batch-event-amount-negative
cases.why: A negative amount is answered error with invalid_amount.

refused.message: Pass amount as a whole number from 1 to 9007199254740991.

cases.name: batch-event-amount-above-largest
cases.why: 2^53 is one more than the largest amount, so the event is answered error with invalid_amount.

refused.message: Pass amount as a whole number from 1 to 9007199254740991.

cases.name: batch-largest-amount
cases.why: 2^53 − 1 is the largest amount, so the event is sent and hashed as that whole number.

cases.name: batch-three-events
cases.why: Three valid events go in one request whose key is batch: and the hash of the three, in order.

cases.name: batch-three-events-resent
cases.why: Sending the same events again sends the same derived key, so the API replays its first answer.

cases.name: batch-rerun-of-last-two-events
cases.why: A rerun of only the last two of batch-three-events' events hashes those two, so its key differs from the first request's.

cases.name: batch-three-events-registering
cases.why: register true takes the register place in the hashed array, so the same events as batch-three-events send another key.

cases.name: batch-occurred-at-as-sent
cases.why: occurredAt is hashed as sent, in UTC with milliseconds whatever offset it was given with, and an event without one hashes null.

cases.name: batch-customers-serialised-unescaped
cases.why: The hashed array escapes only the characters JSON requires, so a slash, a colon and non-ASCII characters stay as they are, while a quote and a backslash are escaped.

cases.name: batch-invalid-event-in-the-middle
cases.why: An invalid event between two valid ones is answered error, and the one request holds and hashes only the two events sent, in order.

refused.message: Pass idempotencyKey as 1 to 200 printable ASCII characters.

cases.name: batch-every-event-refused
cases.why: When every event is refused there is nothing left to send, so the call answers each event error and sends no request.

refused.message: Provide the id your app uses for the customer.
Name the feature by its key.
Pass amount as a whole number from 1 to 9007199254740991.

cases.name: batch-empty
cases.why: An empty input sends nothing and answers no results.

cases.name: batch-501-events-one-refused-one-request
cases.why: Only the events sent count towards the 500 in a request, so 501 events with one refused send a single request of 500.

refused.message: Pass amount as a whole number from 1 to 9007199254740991.

cases.name: batch-event-dots-customer
cases.why: A customer made only of dots is one customer(id) refuses, so the event is answered error with invalid_body and the dots message, and nothing is sent.

refused.message: Pass an id that is not made only of dots.

cases.name: batch-event-single-dot-customer
cases.why: A customer of one dot is refused the same way.

refused.message: Pass an id that is not made only of dots.

cases.name: batch-event-every-field-faulty
cases.why: With every field faulty, the customer's fault is the one answered.

refused.message: Provide the id your app uses for the customer.

cases.name: batch-event-feature-and-amount-faulty
cases.why: The feature's fault comes before the amount's.

refused.message: Name the feature by its key.

cases.name: batch-event-amount-and-key-faulty
cases.why: The amount's fault comes before the key's.

refused.message: Pass amount as a whole number from 1 to 9007199254740991.

cases.name: batch-without-register
cases.why: A batch given no register hashes register as false, so its key equals the same events sent with register false.

cases.name: batch-with-register-false
cases.why: The same events with register false, for comparison with batch-without-register.
